0: Commemoration of the deceased Brethren, Sisters, Relations and Benefactors of our Order.
1: Direct, we beseech thee, O Lord, our actions by thy holy inspiration, and carry them on by thy gracious assistance: that every prayer and work of ours may always begin from thee, and by thee be happily ended.
2: May the heavenly Master instruct us in the discipline of the Rule.
3: Beloved of God and men, whose memory is in benediction: he made him like the saints in glory.
4: ℣. The just shall spring as the lily.
5: ℟. And shall flourish for ever before the Lord.
6: ℟. The just shall flourish like the palm tree * In the house of the Lord.
7: ℟. The Lord conducted the just * Through the right ways.
8: ℣. Let thy mercy, O Lord, be upon us.
9: ℟. As we have hoped in thee.
10: ℣. I will meditate on thee, O Lord, in the morning.
11: ℟. Because thou hast been my helper.
12: Ant. Alleluia. The Lord is risen, alleluia: as he said unto you, alleluia, alleluia.
13: ℣. He shall grow up like the cedar of Libanus.
14: ℣. God hath chosen her, and forechosen her.
15: ℟. He hath made her to dwell in his tabernacle.
16: ℟.br. The just shall flourish like the palm tree * In the house of the Lord.
17: ℟.br. The Lord conducted the just * Through the right ways.
18: ℟. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.
19: Thou dost lay bare the darkness of night,
20: And art believed the light of light,
27: Hold back them that lie in wait,
29: Whom thou hast purchased with thy Blood.
31: Thou who art the defender of the soul,
32: Be present with us, O Lord.
33: ℟. The Lord is risen, * Alleluia, alleluia.
34: ℣. A crown of gold upon his head.
36: ℟. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.
37: And call not anything your own, but let all things be common to you. And let food and clothing be distributed to each of you by your superior, not equally to all, for you are not all equally strong, but rather to each according to his need.
38: Be instant in prayer at the hours and times appointed. In the oratory let no one do anything but that for which it was made and from which it takes its name; so that if any, even outside the appointed hours, should wish to pray there when they are free, they be not hindered by those who think to do something else there. When you pray to God in psalms and hymns, let that be pondered in the heart which is uttered by the mouth.
39: ℣. The Lord is high above all nations.
41: Subdue your flesh by fasting and abstinence from food and drink, as far as health allows. But when anyone cannot fast, let him not take any food outside the hour of the meal, unless he be sick.
42: These, then, are the things which we command you who are established in the monastery to observe. First, since for this you are gathered together in one, that you dwell of one mind in the house, and have one soul and one heart in God.
43: Ant. In the midst of life we are in death: whom do we seek to help us but thee, O Lord, who for our sins art justly angered? * Holy God, holy and mighty, holy and merciful Saviour, deliver us not to bitter death.
44: Have no quarrels, or end them as quickly as you can, lest anger grow into hatred and make a beam out of a mote, and make the soul a murderer. For so you read: Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer.
45: The saints by faith conquered kingdoms, wrought justice, obtained promises, in Christ Jesus our Lord.
46: Ant. At thy coming deliver us, O Lord.
47: Ant. Stir up thy might, O Lord, and come to save us.
48: ℟. It is good for me, O Lord, that thou hast humbled me.
49: ℣. In their hands they shall bear thee up.
50: ℟. Lest thou dash thy foot against a stone.
51: ℣. He shall say to the Lord: Thou art my protector.
52: ℟. Seven times a day I have given praise to thee, O Lord my God.
53: ℟. Holy Mary, Mother of Christ, * Hear thy servants who pray to thee.
54: Ant. O glorious King among thy Saints, who art ever to be praised and yet art ineffable: thou, O Lord, art among us, and thy holy name is called upon us: forsake us not, O our God; that in the day of judgement thou mayest vouchsafe to place us among thy Saints and thine Elect, O blessed King.
55: Qui tecum, Amen, Benedicamus Domino and Fidelium are not said.
56: Ant. Hail, star of the morning, medicine of sinners, princess and queen of the world, the only Virgin worthy to be so called: against the darts of the enemy set the shield of salvation, the title of thy power. O chosen bride of God, be to us the straight way to eternal joys.
57: ℣. Send forth, O Lord, the Lamb, the ruler of the earth.
58: ℟. From Petra of the desert, to the mount of the daughter of Sion.
59: ℟. Princes have persecuted me without cause, and my heart hath been in awe of thy words.
60: ℟. From the lion's mouth deliver me, O Lord.
61: ℟. Deliver, O God, my soul from the sword.
62: Ant. Alleluia. Christ ascending on high, alleluia, led captivity captive, alleluia, alleluia.
63: ℟.br. The Lord is risen, * Alleluia, alleluia.
64: ℣. Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.
65: ℟. The Lord is God, and he hath shone upon us.
66: ℣. He hath made her to dwell in his tabernacle.
67: ℣. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.
68: ℣. And bring down to us from heaven the pardon thou hast obtained.
69: Ant. With heart and soul let us sing glory to Christ, on this holy solemnity of Mary, the exalted Mother of God.
70: Ant. Watch over us, * eternal Saviour, lest the cunning tempter seize us, for thou art made our everlasting helper.
71: Ant. Watch over us, eternal Saviour, lest the cunning tempter seize us, for thou art made our everlasting helper.
72: ℣. Cast us not off in the time of old age; when our strength shall fail, forsake us not, O Lord. Holy God.
73: Ant. Alleluia. The Spirit, the Paraclete, alleluia, will teach you all things, alleluia, alleluia.
74: As the vine I have brought forth a pleasant odour: and my flowers are the fruit of honour and riches.
75: ℣. The declaration of thy words giveth understanding, O Lord.
76: ℟. Show forth thy mercy upon us, O God.
79: * The law of thy mouth is good to me, above thousands of gold and silver.
80: ℣. Thy hands have made me and formed me: give me understanding, and I will learn thy commandments.
81: ℟. The law of thy mouth is good to me, above thousands of gold and silver.
82: ℟. The just shall flourish like the palm tree in the house of the Lord, * Alleluia, alleluia.
83: ℟. The Lord conducted the just through the right ways, * Alleluia, alleluia.
84: ℣. I have gone astray like a sheep that is lost: * seek thy servant, O Lord, because I have not forgotten thy commandments.
85: * That I may keep thy commandments, O Lord.
86: ℣. I have not declined from thy judgements, because thou hast set me a law.
87: ℟. That I may keep thy commandments, O Lord.
88: ℟. Make me a partaker, O God, with all them that fear thee.
90: ℣. Look thou upon me, and have mercy on me, according to the judgement of them that love thy name.
92: ℟. Make me a partaker, O God, with all them that fear thee,
93: ℣. The just shall spring as the lily, alleluia.
94: ℟. And shall flourish for ever before the Lord, alleluia.
95: ℣. Holy Mother of God, Mary ever Virgin.
96: ℟. Intercede for us with the Lord our God.
97: ℟.br. Holy Mary, Mother of Christ, * Hear thy servants who pray to thee.
98: ℟. Hear thy servants who pray to thee.
99: May the Lord grant that you observe all these things as lovers of spiritual beauty, and giving forth the good odour of Christ by your good life: not as servants under the law, but as free men established under grace.
100: Mercifully hear, O God, the supplication of thy servants: that we who are gathered together on the solemnity of the Mother of God and Virgin, may by her intercession be delivered by thee from the dangers that threaten us.
101: Ant. Alleluia. The Word was made flesh, alleluia, and dwelt among us, alleluia, alleluia.
102: ℟. He shall cry to me, * Alleluia, alleluia.
103: Glory be to thee, O Lord,
105: ℟. Thy magnificence is elevated, * Alleluia, alleluia.
106: Give ear, O Lord, to our supplications: that we who know ourselves to be guilty by reason of our iniquity, may be delivered by the intercession of blessed N. thy Martyr.
107: ℟. Thou art become beautiful * And sweet.
108: ℟. After childbirth, O Virgin, * Thou didst remain inviolate.
109: ℣. Attend to my soul, and deliver it.
110: ℟. Save me because of my enemies.
111: * I will rejoice at thy words.
112: ℣. As one that hath found great spoil. I will rejoice at thy words.
113: * And my lowness from the horns of the unicorns.
114: ℣. Deliver, O God, my soul from the sword, my only one from the hand of the dog. And my lowness from the horns of the unicorns.
115: ℣. Save me from the lion's mouth, and my lowness from the horns of the unicorns. And my only one from the hand of the dog.
116: Ant. The souls of the wicked raged against me: and my heart was heavy because of them.
